endorsements.quote: Disclose how and where AI was used (methods/acknowledgments/cover letter), verify all references against primary materials, and ensure no AI system is credited as an author, consistent with ICMJE/WAME/COPE [ 4 - 6 ].

Where health data are involved, enforce strict privacy boundaries: keep protected/identifiable information off public tools, prefer institution-approved solutions under appropriate agreements, and document the legal basis, as in the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and any required approvals (see Table 2 ) [ 1 , 20 ].

Keep protected/identifiable information off public tools; prefer institution-approved solutions under the right agreements (e.g., data processing agreement (DPA)/business associate agreement (BAA); document the legal basis (e.g., GDPR) and any required approvals; and align with local institutional policy [ 1 , 20 ].

To strengthen factual grounding, pair generation with retrieval-augmented workflows restricted to rights-cleared, authoritative sources; recent medicine-specific evaluations, such as the MIRAGE benchmark (Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine), suggest accuracy gains when retrieval is well designed [ 18 , 19 ].
Implement retrieval-augmented workflows so every claim links to retrievable primary sources (DOI (Digital Object Identifier)/PMID (PubMed Identifier)/URL (Uniform Resource Locator)).
Require manual verification for any claim drafted with LLM support.

Define which tasks are appropriate for LLM assistance (e.g., outlining, language refinement, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based summarization) and which are excluded; record this in a governance note and in Table 2 .
Record model/provider, version/date, hosting, and data residency; prompts, parameters, retrieval settings (top-k, ranking, and recency), and timestamps/source IDs; and keep versioned outputs.
Maintain full search strings, databases, dates/limits, de-duplication criteria, and a PRISMA flow with screening logs (see Table 3 ) [ 11 ].
Record performance metrics, calibration/uncertainty, and pre-specified subgroup/fairness analyses [ 13 - 16 ].
Require expert sign-off at key checkpoints: literature selection, data extraction, statistics, and reference verification.

unlisted_practices: Align reporting of AI-enabled trials, prediction models, and systematic reviews with the relevant guideline (CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, DECIDE-AI, TRIPOD+AI, PRISMA 2020) matched to study type.
For high-impact claims, mandate targeted re-reads of the primary sources before submission.
Require two-person dual verification of critical claims and quantitative results with recorded sign-off.

screen.reason: This technical report proposes a framework and structured workflow/checklists for governing and safely adopting LLMs in clinical trials and prediction models, rather than empirically testing an implementation.
